newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tan Chong revises restructuring scheme.
newsitem.headline: Tan Chong revises restructuring scheme.

text.p: Malaysian car assembler Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd on Friday announced a revision of the schemes of arrangement under the proposed rationalisation and demerger of its group operations.

Under the proposed internal reorganisation, the group's local automotive parts, local non-motor and foreign operations divisions would be rationalised and regrouped under three wholly-owned subsidiaries -- APM Automotive Holdings Bhd, Warisan TC Holdings Bhd and Tan Chong International Ltd.
APM and Warisan TC will apply for listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and Tan Chong International on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong, Tan Chong said in a statement.
At the same time, two new companies would be established with Tan Chong's current shareholders holding 40 percent equity interest in each.
The other 60 percent would be held by Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) investors.

Subsequently, Tan Chong would dispose its entire equity in APM after the proposed internal reorganisation to one of the new companies for 779.30 million ringgit to be satisfied by a cash payment of 389.65 million ringgit and an issue of 389.65 million new shares of 1.0 ringgit each.
Tan Chong Motor would also dispose Warisan TC to the other company for 166.78 million ringgit to be satisfied by cash of 83.39 million ringgit and an issue of 83.39 million new shares.

The proposed disposal of APM and Warisan TC by Tan Chong would result in the two new companies becoming subsidiaries of Tan Chong which would hold 50 percent equity interest plus one share in each, the statement said.
Tan Chong would retain its 100 percent equity interest in Tan Chong International.
These investments owned by Tan Chong would be distributed to its existing shareholders on a pro-rata basis by way of a capital repayment.
The cash to be received from the disposal of APM and Warisan TC would also be distributed to shareholders on a pro-rata basis by way of a combination of a repayment of capital and special dividend.
At the end of the revised scheme, Tan Chong's major shareholders would own 45 percent equity interest in both Tan Chong and Tan Chong International, and 42.5 percent in Warisan TC and APM.
